title: A Frog Swallows This Beetle Whole, and It Walks Back Out
subject: water beetle

scenes.text: A frog swallows this beetle whole. Hours later, the beetle walks out alive.
It's a water beetle from Japan, five millimeters long. More than nine in ten survived the trip.
They came out headfirst, most within one to six hours, and kept living for at least two weeks.
How? Researchers think the beetle pokes the frog's gut until the exit relaxes, and out it goes.
The proof: when scientists waxed the beetle's legs together, none of them escaped.
Swallowed alive, and it still leaves through the back door. Frogs never saw that coming.

description:
A pond frog swallows a tiny water beetle whole, and more than nine in ten beetles come back out alive.
The beetle, Regimbartia attenuata, is about 5 millimeters long. In lab tests most were excreted headfirst within one to six hours and lived at least two more weeks. Beetles with their legs waxed together all died, so researchers think the beetle's movement is what triggers the exit.
Would you have believed it? Comment below.
first_comment: A different beetle species, Enochrus japonicus, did not make it out: every one died inside the frog. What is the wildest animal escape you know?
